title: Welcome to Flood-Net
summary: A first look, with Graham and Turbo: the stations, the repeaters and the radio paths between them, in one place — and where to start.

scenes.title: Welcome to Flood-Net
scenes.line: The stations, the repeaters and the radio paths between them — in one place.
scenes.say: G'day. Graham Watts. I've looked after these gauges longer than most of them have been on the air. Let me show you round.

scenes.title: The network
scenes.say: These are the stations that measure the rain and the rivers, and the repeaters that relay their readings home by radio.
scenes.note: Counted from the station list this device has loaded.

scenes.title: On the map
scenes.say: Here they all are, from the coast to well past the range.

scenes.title: The front page
scenes.sub: How the network is, and the tools used most
scenes.say: The front page tells you how the network is right now, and puts the tools you'll reach for most a press away.

callouts.text: How the network is, right now
The tools used most, a press away

scenes.title: A station's card
scenes.say: Press a station and its card has the lot: its health, who owns it, and its rain and river neighbours, their plots a press away.

callouts.text: When it was last heard, and anything wrong
Its river and rain neighbours, plotted

scenes.title: How the network is
scenes.say: Every weekday morning the network checks itself, and the crew put what needs a look into a short bulletin, with one for the whole week on Mondays.

callouts.text: The morning's bulletin, said by the crew

scenes.title: The radio side
scenes.sub: What else is on the air
scenes.say: On the radio side, it lists every licensed transmitter that could trouble a repeater, scored, worst first, with path profiles and coverage on the map.

callouts.text: Each repeater, and what could trouble it
Every licensed transmitter, scored, worst first

scenes.title: Out in the field
scenes.say: Out in the field it's made for your phone: the stations nearest where you're standing, the inspection sheet, and photos that know where they were taken. There's plenty more. Turbo, you're quicker than me.

callouts.text: The stations nearest you, by distance
Press one for its sheet, photos or the way in

scenes.title: And plenty more
scenes.sub: A line each on the Capabilities page
scenes.say: Flat out, then! Path profiles, link budgets, radio coverage, repeater sites, ALERT decoders, bit-flip hunting, interference cases, level surveys, two-peg tests, field photos, printable path maps, and exports for Radio Mobile and Google Earth!

items.text: The best spots for a repeater
Radio Mobile, KML and CSV exports

scenes.title: Where the data comes from
scenes.sub: Every source credited on the Capabilities page
scenes.say: And the data comes in from the Bureau, ACMA, the Queensland Government, Transport and Main Roads, the councils' cameras, Geoscience Australia, New South Wales Spatial Services, the ACCC, OpenStreetMap, Esri and the ECMWF. Personal best!

scenes.title: The rest, a line each
scenes.sub: And where each one comes from
scenes.say: That's the start of it. The lot is listed on one page, a line each, with where each one comes from, and there are short videos for the jobs you'll do most.

scenes.title: Have a look round
scenes.say: Have a look round. It's going to be a long day, so we might as well do it properly.
scenes.line: Might as well do it properly.
